whyEn: Chapter 4 told you what the law can punish; this chapter trains the judgment for the calls where the law is silent. The exam pulls a small, predictable set of structures from it: the four principles of Beauchamp and Childress (autonomy, beneficence, nonmalfeasance, justice), the persuasion–coercion–manipulation distinction in consent, the five situations that justify withholding or withdrawing care, when not to start and when to stop resuscitation, and the escalation ladder for a colleague's misconduct. The deeper payoff is bigger than the one or two written questions: the ethical reflex — 'what is in the best interest of the patient?' — is the tiebreaker the practical exam expects to see behind every consent, refusal, triage, and end-of-life decision you make.
whyZh: 第 4 章讲的是法律能惩罚什么，这一章训练的是法律沉默时的判断力。笔试从中抽取的结构小而可预测：Beauchamp 与 Childress 四原则（自主、行善、不伤害、公正）、同意里说服／胁迫／操纵的三分界线、可以不给或撤除治疗的五种情形、什么时候不启动复苏与什么时候终止复苏、以及同事失当行为的逐级处理阶梯。但真正的回报比那一两道笔试题大得多：『怎样做对患者最有利？』这条伦理反射弧，正是实操考期待在你每一次同意、拒绝、分诊与临终决策背后看到的裁决准则。

sections.titleEn: Medical Ethics: Definitions and the Four Principles
sections.titleZh: 医学伦理：定义与四大原则

points.en: Three words the exam wants kept apart: ethics is the philosophy of right and wrong, moral duties, and ideal professional behaviour; morality is a code of conduct defined by society, religion, culture, or another person, shaping character and conscience; and medical ethics (bioethics) is the discipline within ethics that debates the dilemmas arising in patient care. Law, from Chapter 4, differs from all three by carrying enforceable sanctions.
points.zh: 考试要求分开的三个词：伦理（ethics）是关于对错、道德义务与理想职业行为的哲学；道德（morality）是由社会、宗教、文化或他人定义的行为准则，塑造品格与良知；医学伦理（bioethics）则是伦理学内部专门讨论医疗照护困境的分支。而第 4 章讲过的法律与这三者的区别在于：法律带有可强制执行的制裁。

points.en: Many ethical theories exist — deontological, utilitarian, virtue, care, relativism, egalitarian, libertarian, feminist — and the book's verdict on all of them is the same: no single theory can answer every dilemma or uniformly guide professional conduct. That is exactly why a working framework matters more than a favourite philosophy.
points.zh: 伦理理论琳琅满目——义务论、功利主义、德性伦理、关怀伦理、相对主义、平等主义、自由至上主义、女性主义——原书对它们的判词只有一句：没有任何单一理论能解答所有困境、统一指导职业行为。这正是『一套可操作的框架』比『一个心仪的哲学流派』更重要的原因。

points.en: Principlism — Beauchamp and Childress, 1979 — holds that four equally important principles run through all ethical theories: autonomy, respecting people's right to make capable, informed decisions about their own health care; beneficence, doing what is best for the patient; nonmalfeasance, the creed of primum non nocere — first, do no harm; and justice, fairness — 'treat equal cases equally and unequal cases unequally' — including how health care resources are distributed.
points.zh: 原则主义——Beauchamp 与 Childress，1979 年——认为四条同等重要的原则贯穿所有伦理理论：自主（autonomy），尊重每个人对自身医疗作出有能力的知情决定的权利；行善（beneficence），做对患者最有利的事；不伤害（nonmalfeasance），即 primum non nocere——首先，不伤害；公正（justice），公平对待——『相同的情形同等对待，不同的情形区别对待』——其中包含医疗资源如何分配的考量。

points.en: The four principles are a framework, not a formula: they can conflict with one another, and respecting different principles may point to markedly different actions. Their value is in unpacking a dilemma, analyzing it from several perspectives, and building a resolution — not in dispensing automatic answers.
points.zh: 四原则是框架，不是公式：它们彼此会打架，尊重不同的原则可能指向截然不同的做法。它们的价值在于把困境拆开、从多个视角分析、再搭出解决方案——而不是自动吐出标准答案。

points.en: Know thyself is a professional duty: everyone carries different beliefs, values, cultural and religious backgrounds, and experiences, and assuming your patient shares your moral standards is frequently false. Your standards may even conflict with the patient's wishes or best interests — the fiduciary duty of a paramedic is to put the patient's interests before your own.
points.zh: 『认识你自己』在这里是职业义务：每个人的信念、价值观、文化宗教背景和阅历都不同，默认患者和你共享同一套道德标准往往是错的。你的标准甚至可能与患者的意愿或最佳利益相冲突——救护员的受信义务（fiduciary duty）就是把患者的利益放在自己的前面。

points.en: The Declaration of Geneva — first drafted by the World Medical Association in 1948, and still the oath many medical graduates take — is the book's exemplar code of ethics. Its testable clauses: the health of my patient will be my first consideration; I will respect the secrets confided in me even after the patient has died; no consideration of age, disease or disability, creed, ethnic origin, gender, nationality, political affiliation, race, sexual orientation, or social standing may come between my duty and my patient; and I will not use my medical knowledge to violate human rights and civil liberties, even under threat.
points.zh: 《日内瓦宣言》——世界医学会 1948 年首次起草，至今仍是许多医学毕业生宣读的誓词——是原书树立的伦理守则范本。可考的条款：患者的健康是我的首要考虑；我将尊重托付给我的秘密，即使在患者去世之后；不允许年龄、疾病或残障、信仰、族裔、性别、国籍、政治立场、种族、性取向、社会地位等任何因素横在我的职责与患者之间；即使受到威胁，我也绝不用我的医学知识去侵犯人权与公民自由。

points.en: The NOCP lists ethical behaviour among the first professional behaviours a paramedic must understand, value, and integrate. The working compass: your first priority is concern for the welfare of others, and each time right and wrong collide, ask 'what is in the best interest of the patient?' — place that ahead of everything else and you will rarely, if ever, commit an unethical act.
points.zh: NOCP 把伦理行为列在救护员必须理解、珍视并融入执业的首批职业行为之中。可用的罗盘只有一枚：首要关切是他人的福祉；每当对与错相撞，就问『怎样做对患者最有利？』——把这个问题摆在一切之前，你几乎不可能做出不合伦理的事。

points.en: Paramedics are accountable to more systems than the average health care provider: the regional paramedic system, the medical director, the employer, and the community's standard of care can all compete with the patient's wishes. When those interests collide, the resolution runs through communication with every party involved — not through silently picking a master.
points.zh: 救护员要向比一般医疗人员更多的系统交账：区域急救体系、医疗主任、雇主、社区的照护标准，都可能与患者本人的意愿相互竞争。利益相撞时，出路是与所有相关方沟通协调——而不是默默挑一个『主子』听命。

sections.titleEn: Patient Autonomy: Capacity, Consent, Advance Care, MAID
sections.titleZh: 患者自主：能力、同意、预立照护与医疗协助死亡

points.en: Autonomy — the patient's right to direct their own care, including end-of-life care — is the front-line principle of modern medical ethics. Respecting it means seeing each patient as a unique person with deeply held values and past experiences behind their decisions, never as 'another case of X'; and that respect is itself therapeutic, building trust and showing the caring and empathy of high-quality care when people need it most.
points.zh: 自主权——患者主导自身医疗（包括临终医疗）的权利——是当代医学伦理的头号原则。尊重它，意味着把每位患者当成一个带着深层价值观和人生经历来做决定的独特的人，而不是『又一个某某病例』；这份尊重本身就有疗愈作用——在人最需要的时刻建立信任，呈现高质量照护里的关怀与同理。

points.en: Capacity is presumed, and it has exactly two testable components: the ability to (1) understand information about one's state of health and treatment options, and (2) appreciate the consequences of a decision — or of making no decision. A capable patient may accept or refuse treatment according to, or even against, the provider's advice — including refusing effective and even life-sustaining options.
points.zh: 行为能力默认存在，而它恰好由两个可考的部件组成：①理解自身健康状况与治疗选项相关信息的能力；②领会某个决定——或不做决定——会带来什么后果的能力。有能力的患者可以听从、也可以违逆医疗建议接受或拒绝治疗——包括拒绝有效的、甚至维持生命的治疗。

points.en: Capacity is a moving target: it shifts with physical, psychological, and emotional state and with medications — prescription, over-the-counter, or street drugs. A patient can be capable of consenting to one treatment yet incapable for a more complex one, and some patients understand a treatment but cannot appreciate the consequences of their choice. So assess capacity when the care relationship begins, reassess as the condition changes — and the moment capacity returns, the patient takes back control of every decision.
points.zh: 行为能力是个移动靶：它随身体、心理、情绪状态起伏，也被药物左右——处方药、非处方药、毒品都算。患者可能对一种治疗有同意能力，对另一种更复杂的治疗却没有；也有人听懂了治疗本身，却领会不了选择的后果。所以在建立照护关系时就要评估能力，病情变化时反复评估——而能力一旦恢复，患者立刻收回全部决定权。

points.en: The consent rules of this chapter, ethically framed: in an emergency with an incapable patient, consent is presumed — err on the side of life and initiate all required resuscitation, then obtain consent to continue at the earliest opportunity from the recovered patient or their substitute decision maker. In every nonemergency, consent comes first, even for paramedic treatment. Valid consent requires three ethical conditions: a capable patient (or their legal substitute if incapable), informed, and voluntary — free of coercion and manipulation.
points.zh: 本章从伦理角度重述的同意规则：紧急情况下患者无能力时，同意被推定——宁可偏向抢救生命，先启动一切必要的复苏，再在第一时间向恢复能力的患者或其替代决策人取得继续治疗的同意。所有非紧急情形，先有同意才有治疗，救护员的处置也不例外。有效同意需要三个伦理条件：患者有能力（无能力时由法定替代决策人给出）、知情、自愿——不受胁迫与操纵。

points.en: 'Informed' is measured against the reasonable person in the patient's circumstances, plus time and space for questions. The full disclosure list: why treatment is needed, the recommended option and its alternatives; expected benefits and their likelihood; material risks and their likelihood; material side effects and their likelihood; what further treatment those risks or side effects would require; the likely consequences of declining; the provider's recommendation among the options; and answers to whatever the patient or substitute asks. Legally the consent may be expressed — oral or written — or implied, as when the patient sticks out an arm for the IV.
points.zh: 『知情』的标尺是『处于患者境地的理性人想知道什么』，还要留出提问的时间与机会。完整的告知清单：为什么需要治疗、推荐方案与替代方案；预期益处及其实现概率；重大风险及其发生概率；重大副作用及其发生概率；风险或副作用真出现时还需要什么后续治疗；不治疗的可能后果；在各选项中你为何如此推荐；以及回答患者或其替代决策人提出的任何问题。法律形式上，同意可以是明示的（口头或书面），也可以是默示的——比如患者主动伸出胳膊让你扎针。

points.en: Persuasion, coercion, manipulation — one is ethical, two are forbidden, and the exam tests the line. Persuasion appeals honestly: 'I really feel you should come to the hospital; we are concerned about you.' Coercion threatens: 'If you don't come, we will never respond to your 9-1-1 call again.' Manipulation distorts: 'If you don't come, chances are great you will die in the next 5 minutes.' The ends never justify the means — even when you are genuinely acting in the patient's best interests.
points.zh: 说服、胁迫、操纵——一个合乎伦理，两个被禁止，考试就考这条线。说服是诚实的劝告：『我真的觉得你该去医院，我们都很担心你。』胁迫是威胁：『你不去，以后你打 911 我们就再也不来了。』操纵是扭曲事实：『你不去，五分钟内八成就没命了。』目的永远不能为手段开脱——哪怕你真心在为患者好。

points.en: Advance care planning is a capable patient expressing wishes — oral or written — about future care and expected quality of life; the wishes themselves are advance directives. Three rules govern them: they take effect only once the patient loses capacity; they never replace obtaining consent at the actual time of treatment (that conversation reviews values, corrects misconceptions, and updates goals); and the most current expression of the patient's wishes wins — a capable patient may change a directive at any time, spoken or written, and the change is legally valid. Their weakness: vague language that fails to anticipate real situations, sometimes impossible to apply to the condition at hand.
points.zh: 预立照护计划＝有能力的患者以口头或书面形式，预先表达对未来医疗和期望生活质量的意愿；这些意愿本身就叫预立指示。三条规则管着它：只在患者丧失能力后才生效；它不能取代治疗当时的知情同意（那次对话正是复核价值观、纠正误解、更新目标的机会）；以最新表达为准——有能力的患者随时可以更改指示，口头书面均可，改了就有法律效力。它的软肋：措辞含糊、预想不到真实场景，有时对当下的病情根本无法执行。

points.en: Document taxonomy the exam likes to tangle: an advance directive is not a DNR order — the directive is what lets decisions like a DNR be consented to once the patient is incapacitated. A power of attorney for personal care is a formal legal document that may contain advance directives and appoints an attorney for personal care (a substitute decision maker) — who need not be a relative, only someone close who understands the patient's wishes. And neither the attorney for financial matters nor the executor of the estate automatically gains any health care decision power.
points.zh: 考试爱搅混的文件分类学：预立指示不是 DNR 指令——指示是让 DNR 这类决定在患者失能后得以被『同意』的载体。个人照护授权书（power of attorney for personal care）是正式法律文件，可以包含预立指示，并指定一位个人照护代理人（即替代决策人）——不必是亲属，只要是了解患者心愿的亲近之人。而财务代理人和遗产执行人，都不会自动获得任何医疗决策权。

points.en: A substitute decision maker arises three ways: designated by the patient orally or in writing; appointed in a power-of-attorney document; or, depending on jurisdiction, by a default family hierarchy beginning with the spouse or partner. You owe the substitute the same explanations you would give the patient. Their decision rule: follow the patient's previously expressed applicable wishes; if none exist, decide by best interests — which is not your personal moral code but a four-part test: the patient's own values, beliefs, and goals; whether treatment would improve condition or quality of life, or slow or prevent deterioration; whether benefits outweigh risks; and whether a less-intrusive plan could achieve the same outcome.
points.zh: 替代决策人有三条产生途径：患者口头或书面指定；在授权书文件里任命；或按辖区规则，依家庭成员的默认顺位——从配偶/伴侣排起。你对替代决策人负有与对患者本人同样的解释义务。他的决策规则：优先执行患者先前表达过、适用于当下的意愿；没有这种意愿时，按最佳利益决定——而最佳利益不是你个人的道德准则，是四步检验：患者自身的价值观、信念与目标；治疗能否改善病情或生活质量、或延缓乃至阻止恶化；收益是否大于风险；有没有更低侵入性的方案能达到同样结果。

points.en: End-of-life calls: never let 'why did they call 9-1-1 if they don't want anything done?' cross your mind — that is your moral code elbowing out your medical ethics. The family of a dying patient may not know how to check a pulse, may not know agonal gasps can continue for hours, and may dial for help at the moment of death simply because they do not know what else to do. If information and support are what they need, providing them is part of your job. Whether palliative-instead-of-resuscitative plans can be legally honoured by paramedics varies by jurisdiction — learn yours.
points.zh: 临终出勤：永远别让『不想抢救干嘛还打 911？』这句话冒头——那是你的个人道德在挤开你的医学伦理。垂死患者的家属可能不会摸脉搏，不知道濒死叹息样呼吸能持续数小时，也可能在亲人咽气那一刻因为不知所措而拨了电话。如果他们需要的是信息和安抚，提供它们就是你分内的工作。至于救护员能否在法律上执行『只姑息、不复苏』的方案，各辖区不一——把你所在辖区的规则学清楚。

points.en: Medical assistance in dying, the timeline and the definition: in February 2015 the Supreme Court of Canada struck down the federal prohibition on physician-assisted dying as a violation of the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, and in June 2016 Parliament passed Bill C-14. The Criminal Code defines MAID two ways: a medical or nurse practitioner administering a substance at a person's request that causes death, or prescribing/providing a substance for the person to self-administer with the same effect — legal only when eligibility criteria are met and procedural safeguards followed.
points.zh: 医疗协助死亡（MAID）的时间线与定义：2015 年 2 月，加拿大最高法院裁定联邦对医助死亡的禁令违反《权利与自由宪章》而将其推翻；2016 年 6 月，国会通过 C-14 法案。《刑法典》给 MAID 下了两种定义：由医师或执业护士应本人请求施用致死药物；或由其开具/提供药物，供本人自行服用而致死——只有在符合资格标准、遵守程序保障时才合法。

points.en: MAID eligibility under Bill C-14 — five criteria, all required: eligible for government-funded health insurance in Canada; 18 years or older; a grievous and irremediable condition; a voluntary request free of external pressure; and informed consent given after being told of the available means to relieve suffering, including palliative care. 'Grievous and irremediable' itself has four components: serious and incurable illness, disease, or disability; an advanced state of irreversible decline in capability; physical and psychological suffering intolerable to the person; and a reasonably foreseeable natural death. Eligibility is assessed by two independent health care professionals, and the person must still be able to give informed consent at the time MAID is performed.
points.zh: C-14 法案下的 MAID 资格——五项标准缺一不可：有资格享受加拿大政府资助的医保；年满 18 岁；患有严重且不可挽回的疾患；请求出于自愿、无外部压力；在被告知包括姑息治疗在内的各种减轻痛苦手段之后给出知情同意。『严重且不可挽回』本身又有四个构件：严重且无法治愈的疾病或残障；能力处于不可逆衰退的晚期；本人无法忍受的身心痛苦；自然死亡已可合理预见。资格须由两名独立的医疗专业人员评估，且在执行 MAID 的当下，本人仍须具备给出知情同意的能力。

points.en: Paramedics rarely deliver MAID but may arrive where it is in progress or complete: respond as you would to any call, honour the patient's expressed wishes and any directives or end-of-life decisions in place, never let the care standard slip merely because the patient is palliative or undergoing MAID, politely ask how you can assist given the process — and when anything is unclear on arrival, consult direct medical control.
points.zh: 救护员几乎不会亲手执行 MAID，但可能到达一个 MAID 正在进行或刚刚完成的现场：像对待任何出勤一样响应；尊重患者已表达的意愿和现有的预立指示、临终决定；绝不因为患者是姑息状态或正在接受 MAID 就降低照护水准；礼貌地询问在这个过程里你能帮上什么——到场后有任何疑问，就请示直接医疗控制。

points.en: DNR orders are recognized prehospital in most if not all jurisdictions, resting on one ethical claim: patients hold the same rights to direct and refuse care outside the hospital as inside it. But the legal frame is not always clean — some places mandate field resuscitation despite clearly expressed contrary wishes, and some allow discontinuation only on the authority of the base hospital physician. Know your system's protocols, and when resuscitation meets uncertainty, call direct medical control.
points.zh: DNR 指令在绝大多数辖区的院前环境都被承认，理据只有一条：患者在医院外享有与院内完全相同的主导和拒绝医疗的权利。但法律框架未必干净利落——有的辖区即便面对明确的相反意愿仍强制现场复苏，有的只允许凭基地医院医生的授权终止复苏。吃透本系统的协议；复苏遇上不确定时，呼叫直接医疗控制。

points.en: Futile interventions — ones studies show do not benefit patients — are neither medically nor ethically indicated. But 'futility' is a dangerous word: definitions lack consensus, saying it to families implies the patient is not worth the effort, and it hands providers a channel to impose their own values about what counts as benefit. The book's fix is a deliberately narrow definition: a treatment is futile if it would not work.
points.zh: 无效干预——研究已证明对患者无益的干预——在医学上和伦理上都没有指征。但『无效（futility）』是个危险的词：医学界对定义并无共识；对家属说出口，等于暗示患者不值得抢救；它还给了医疗人员一条把自己对『什么算获益』的价值观强加于人的通道。原书的解法是把定义收到最窄：治疗无效＝这个治疗不会起作用。

points.en: Five circumstances justify withholding or withdrawing a treatment: (1) the patient or their substitute decision maker requests it; (2) the treatment has not attained its preset goals; (3) the treatment is not working; (4) the burdens exceed the benefits and the patient or substitute consents to stopping; (5) the treatment falls outside a well-recognized, accepted standard of prehospital care. In doubt, contact your medical oversight physician for orders and advice.
points.zh: 五种情形可以正当地不给或撤除治疗：①患者或其替代决策人提出请求；②治疗没有达到预定目标；③治疗不起作用；④负担大于收益，且患者或替代决策人同意停止；⑤该治疗超出了公认的院前照护标准。拿不准时，联系医疗监督医生请求医嘱和建议。

points.en: Slow codes — also called Hollywood codes — are resuscitations run deliberately slowly and inadequately, staged for the family's benefit. They are completely unethical and must never occur: a patient is either resuscitated to the best of your professional ability, or efforts are withheld or stopped in consultation with direct medical control. There is no third mode.
points.zh: 慢代码（slow code）——又叫好莱坞代码——指故意做得又慢又不到位、演给家属看的复苏。这是彻底违背伦理的行为，绝不允许发生：要么以你全部的专业能力全力复苏，要么在与直接医疗控制协商后不启动或终止。没有第三种档位。

points.en: Where the law draws bright lines: do not attempt resuscitation on the obviously dead — livor mortis, rigor mortis, putrefaction — or on injuries incompatible with life, such as decapitation. Field termination of efforts already started may be appropriate in blunt trauma arrest, prolonged rescue or response times, or lengthy medical resuscitations. Who may pronounce death varies by jurisdiction — a paramedic in some, only a medical investigator or physician in others — and local law keeps governing your practice even after the patient is clinically deceased.
points.zh: 法律画出的亮线：对明显死亡者——尸斑、尸僵、腐败——或存在与生命不相容的损伤者（如断头），不启动复苏。已开始的复苏，在钝性创伤心搏骤停、救援或响应时间过长、内科复苏已久无果时，可考虑现场终止。宣告死亡的权限因辖区而异——有的省救护员可以宣告，有的只有法医调查员或医生才行——而且患者临床死亡之后，当地法律依然管着你的每一步操作。

points.en: Resuscitation decisions sit inside resource decisions: EMS resources are finite, and a long transport takes your unit out of service. Use resources to serve the greatest need first, to do the most good for the most people, and to preserve the most coverage at all times — with the scenarios pre-written into protocols and standing discussions with your medical director. In rural and wilderness work, weigh time-to-definitive-care against survival odds; when communication is cut off by terrain, your pre-learned knowledge of interventions and their consequences is what substitutes for direct medical control. Any doubt, any time: err on the side of starting resuscitation.
points.zh: 复苏决策嵌在资源决策里：EMS 资源是有限的，一趟长途转运就让你的车退出待命。资源要用来先救需求最迫切的人、为社区里最多的人做最多的好事、并始终保住最大的覆盖面——这些情形应事先写进协议，并与医疗主任保持常态化讨论。在乡村与荒野环境里，要把『到达确定性治疗的时间』和『生存概率』放在一起掂量；地形阻断通讯时，事先学透各种干预及其后果，就是你对『直接医疗控制』的替代品。任何时候只要有疑问：宁可启动复苏。

points.en: Terminating a pediatric resuscitation is the hardest call in the chapter — studies show paramedics feel distinctly uncomfortable stopping in children, because action-oriented people feel they must do something. The ethical reframe: sometimes you can do more for the grieving family than for the child who has died, and being prepared to support that family is part of the job — often the hardest part. Discuss start-and-stop criteria with your partner before the call, so everyone understands the direction of the resuscitation.
points.zh: 终止儿童复苏是全章最难下的决定——研究显示救护员对给孩子停手格外抗拒，因为行动导向的人总觉得必须做点什么。伦理上的换位：有时你能为悲恸的家庭做的，比为已经离世的孩子能做的更多——准备好去支撑这个家庭，本身就是工作的一部分，往往也是最难的部分。何时开始、何时停止 CPR，出勤前就和搭档讨论清楚，让所有人对复苏的走向心里有数。

sections.titleEn: Conflicts in Professional Integrity and Roles
sections.titleZh: 职业操守与角色的冲突

points.en: When a physician's order strikes you as detrimental to the patient — a procedure you are not trained in, a dose well outside your protocol range — the rule has two halves: never perform a procedure or give a medication you believe will harm the patient, and immediately tell the physician why. You are often the one actually seeing the patient, and full communication is part of your job.
points.zh: 当医生的医嘱在你看来会伤害患者——让你做没受过训练的操作、给出远超协议范围的剂量——规则分两半：绝不执行你认为会伤害患者的操作或给药；同时立刻向医生说明你为什么这样判断。真正守在患者跟前的往往是你，把情况充分沟通出去本来就是你的职责。

points.en: The escalation toolkit for an order you cannot follow: ask the physician for clarification and voice your objection; point to your current standing orders; offer a feasible alternative within your scope of practice; or ask the physician to speak directly with your medical director. Whatever route the conflict takes, your role never changes — act in the patient's best interest as their advocate.
points.zh: 面对执行不了的医嘱，升级工具箱有四件：请医生澄清并陈述异议；亮出你现行的 standing orders；提出一个你执业范围内可行的替代方案；或请这位医生直接与你的医疗主任对话。无论冲突走哪条路，你的角色始终不变——作为患者的代言人，为其最佳利益行事。

points.en: The consent hierarchy that surprises students: even when the patient carries a signed organ and tissue donor card, the actual decision to donate is presented to the family — and if the family refuses, their wishes are respected. It looks like a violation of the patient's autonomy, and the book names the reason: it is done out of respect for the surviving family members. Historically, neurologic (brain) death had to be declared before a patient could be considered a donor and the family approached; donation-after-cardiac-death programs — usually following a decision to withdraw life support in the ICU — are now increasingly available, and some programs controversially explore keeping a brain-dead patient on support until organs can be donated after the subsequent cardiac death.
points.zh: 让考生意外的同意顺位：即使患者签了器官与组织捐献卡，捐与不捐的实际决定仍然交给家属——家属拒绝，就尊重家属。这看似违背了患者的自主意愿，原书点明了理由：这是出于对在世家人的尊重。历史上，须先宣告神经学死亡（脑死亡），患者才能被视为潜在捐献者、家属才能被问及捐献；如今心死亡后捐献项目——通常发生在 ICU 决定撤除生命支持之后——日益普及，还有些项目更具争议地探索：对已进入脑死亡的患者继续维持生命支持，以便在随后的心死亡发生后完成器官与组织捐献。

points.en: The paramedic's slot in the donation pipeline is deliberately small: you are not expected to judge whether organs are viable. Under some systems' protocols — applicable only when resuscitation was terminated in the field or never attempted, and only after criteria such as age, comorbidities, and time of death are met — your part is to tell the next of kin that donation is an option, hand them an information card, and notify the medical examiner or tissue donation service that the conversation has been opened. Enter such conversations only if your service has a protocol for it, and never pressure the family: you provide information, nothing more.
points.zh: 救护员在捐献链条里的位置被刻意设计得很小：不需要你判断器官是否适合移植。在部分系统的协议下——仅适用于复苏已在现场终止或根本未启动的情形，且须先满足年龄、基础疾病、死亡时间等标准——你的角色只是：告知近亲『捐献是一个选项』，递上一张信息卡，然后通知法医或组织捐献机构『这场对话已经开启』。只有在本服务有协议或指南时才进入这类对话，而且永远不给家属施压：你提供的是信息，仅此而已。

points.en: Historically, paramedic practice ran on expert opinion because sound prehospital research was scarce — and some well-intentioned EMS procedures have proven unhelpful to patients. The ethical duty that follows: know which procedures are no longer recommended, even if they anecdotally 'worked' for you or your colleagues in the past, and keep educating yourself on the effectiveness of EMS practice — do-no-harm demands evidence, not habit.
points.zh: 救护实践在历史上长期靠专家意见撑着，因为可靠的院前研究太少——而一些出发点很好的 EMS 操作，最终被证明对患者并无帮助。由此产生的伦理义务：清楚哪些操作已不再被推荐，哪怕它们在你或同事的个人经验里『管用过』；并持续学习 EMS 实践的疗效证据——『不伤害』要求的是证据，不是习惯。

points.en: The core dilemma of prehospital research: studying critically ill or injured patients who cannot consent — unconscious, or so compromised that even a responsive patient cannot absorb enough information for informed consent. Canada's answer is the Tri-Council Policy Statement (TCPS) on Ethical Conduct for Research Involving Humans, which expresses respect for human dignity through three core principles — respect for persons, concern for welfare, and justice — and details how a trial may proceed under a waiver of informed consent. If your service joins such a trial, the waiver means the investigators have satisfied every ethical safeguard; your part is to stay aware of what prehospital research is running and how its ethical issues are being handled.
points.zh: 院前科研的核心两难：研究对象是无法给出同意的危重伤病患者——要么昏迷，要么虚弱到即使有反应也无法消化信息、给不出知情同意。加拿大的答案是《三理事会政策声明》（TCPS，关于涉及人类的研究之伦理行为），它把对人的尊严的尊重落成三条核心原则——尊重人、关切福祉、公正——并详细规定了试验如何在豁免知情同意的条件下进行。你的服务若参与这类试验，『豁免』本身就意味着研究者已把所有伦理保障做到位；你要做的是持续了解正在进行的院前研究，以及研究者如何处理其中的伦理问题。

points.en: The catalogue of conduct that is both unethical and illegal: sexual misconduct, substance abuse, patient abuse, and harassment or stalking of colleagues. Strictly forbidden on top of those: inappropriate use of emergency vehicles, inappropriate visitors entertained at the station, and alcohol on duty. Off-duty misconduct counts too — it damages your reputation, can cost your employment, and every news story of paramedics behaving badly drains public confidence from the entire profession, which is still fighting to be recognized and funded like the other medical professions.
points.zh: 既违伦理又违法的行为清单：性行为不端、物质滥用、虐待患者、骚扰或跟踪同事。在此之上被严格禁止的还有：滥用急救车辆、在站里招待不合适的访客、当班饮酒。下班后的不当行为同样算数——它毁你的名声、可能砸你的饭碗，而每一条『救护员行为不端』的新闻都在抽走公众对整个行业的信任——这个行业还在为获得与其他医疗职业同等的承认和经费而奋斗。

points.en: Falsifying training or certification — misrepresenting your certification level or forging training records — is a named ethical-legal problem in EMS. The practitioner faces charges, and any EMS instructor who signs off on the falsification faces the same; penalties run from suspension and revocation of registration or licensure all the way to criminal and civil charges depending on the patient's outcome.
points.zh: 伪造训练或认证记录——虚报自己的认证级别、造假训练档案——是 EMS 里被点名的伦理法律问题。造假的执业者要被追责，而在造假材料上签字放行的教官同罪；处罚从注册或执照的吊扣、吊销起步，视患者的结局可一路升级到刑事与民事指控。

points.en: The silence rule: you cannot stand by and watch another paramedic's misbehaviour — you are ethically required to disclose it, promptly, up the appropriate chain of command. The same obligation covers medical errors: report those you make or witness to the medical director as soon as possible. Concealing a mistake or omission in patient care is never acceptable, because the cover-up itself can jeopardize the patient's life.
points.zh: 关于沉默的规则：你不能袖手旁观其他救护员的不当行为——伦理上你必须揭露它，及时、沿着正确的指挥链上报。同样的义务覆盖医疗差错：无论是你犯的还是你目击的，都要尽快报告医疗主任。掩盖救治中的错误或疏漏在任何情况下都不可接受——因为掩盖本身就可能危及患者的生命。

points.en: The whistle-blower scenario, resolved by the chapter case: a colleague confides that evidence was destroyed and fears retaliation. Your moves — keep the informant's name private, report the information immediately to your supervisor and medical program director so corrective action can begin, and tell the informant honestly what you must do while promising to protect their identity. Doing the right thing can carry personal costs — a lost job, a whistle-blower reputation — but looking the other way makes you a party to the misconduct, and your duty runs to your patients, your community, and your profession.
points.zh: 吹哨人情境，本章案例给出的解法：同事私下告诉你有人销毁了证据，又怕被报复。你的动作——为线人保密姓名；立即把信息报给主管和医疗项目主任，让纠正程序启动；坦诚告知线人你必须走哪些程序，同时承诺保护他的身份。做正确的事可能有个人代价——丢掉工作、背上『吹哨人』的名声——但视而不见就等于成了不当行为的同伙，而你的义务对象是患者、社区和这个职业。

points.en: Honesty with families under pressure: when the wife of an arrested patient asks why the AED failed, do not lie — give facts, stick to what you know, and if you do not know, say so and promise to find out. But timing and setting matter: while you are actively caring for her husband is not the moment; ideally a physician explains complications later, somewhere quiet, private, and less stressful. Follow your service's guidelines for family interactions — and where none exist, common sense and sensitivity fill the gap.
points.zh: 高压之下对家属的诚实：骤停患者的妻子问 AED 为什么没能用，不许撒谎——只讲事实、只说你确知的部分；不知道就承认不知道，并承诺去查清后给她准确答复。但时机和场合同样重要：你还在全力抢救她丈夫的当口不是谈这件事的时候；理想做法是事后由医生在安静、私密、压力小的环境里解释并发症。与家属的互动照本服务的规程走——没有规程的地方，用常识和体恤补位。

points.en: Sensitive information needs a discreet channel: never ignore an incoming crew's radio questions, but for minors, sexual assault, child abuse, and similar situations, switch to a landline or cellular phone — or at minimum radio that the details will come face-to-face. Going silent instead leaves the receiving crew wondering whether the radio failed, they are being ignored, or something is wrong.
points.zh: 敏感信息要走谨慎的通道：对接收车组的电台询问绝不能置之不理，但涉及未成年人、性侵、儿童虐待等情形时，改用座机或手机——至少也要在电台里说一句『细节见面再谈』。若干脆沉默，对方只会猜测是电台坏了、被你无视了、还是出了什么事。

points.en: When an incident goes wrong, two documents exist: the medical incident report, and a separate typed addendum or memo not attached to it — holding the information that does not belong in a medical record: provider comments, scene conditions, details likely to be forgotten later. Include names, dates, times, witnesses, and references to other documents; stick to facts; and write it knowing it could be subpoenaed. The broader documentation creed: misspellings, illegible handwriting, and omissions all say 'not a professional,' and a jury may one day be invited to agree that poor documentation meant poor care.
points.zh: 事件出了岔子，文书要有两份：医疗事件报告本身，以及一份单独打印、不附在报告上的补充备忘——收纳不适合写进医疗文书的信息：其他人员的说法、现场状况、日后容易遗忘的细节。写上姓名、日期、时间、见证人和相关文件的索引；只写事实；并且落笔时就当它有朝一日会被传唤为证据。更大的文书信条：拼写错误、字迹潦草、内容缺漏都在宣告『此人不专业』，而陪审团某天可能被引导得出『文书烂＝救治也烂』的结论。

points.en: Three system-level answers from the case summary: (1) quality assurance and improvement exist to keep paramedics on track — informal and formal review of all calls, flagging those needing scrutiny, under the oversight physician whose licence you work under; (2) EMRs and volunteer crews should ideally be held to the same care standards as staff paramedics — the family cannot tell who is paid, and professionalism (equipment known, clean and ready, adequate supplies, clean uniform and unit) is owed regardless; (3) both individuals and departments can be sued, civilly and criminally — never assume your service's insurance covers your personal legal costs; know your coverage, and consider a separate personal policy.
points.zh: 案例总结给出的三个系统层面的答案：①质量保证与质量改进的目的就是让救护员不跑偏——用非正式加正式的机制复盘所有出勤、标记需要审查的案例，一切在你所挂靠执照的监督医生之下运转；②EMR 和志愿车组理应与在编救护员执行同一套照护标准——患者家属分不清谁领工资，而专业素养（设备了然于胸、清洁待命、物资充足、制服和车辆干净）是无条件欠着的；③个人和部门都可能被告上民事与刑事法庭——别想当然认为单位的保险会替你付个人律师费；弄清你的保障范围，必要时自购一份独立保单。

points.en: The chapter's career close: paramedics who become patient advocates, chase the best training and professional development, and put the team's good above personal ambition are the ones rewarded with a fulfilling career — and good ethics are instilled by good mentors, so find one whose style and professionalism you want to emulate.
points.zh: 全章的职业收束：那些甘当患者代言人、主动追求最好的训练与职业发展、把团队利益放在个人抱负之上的救护员，最终会收获充实的职业生涯——而好的伦理是由好的导师传下来的，所以去找一位风格与专业素养都值得你效仿的引路人。

atScene.en: Many provinces and territories have legislation for powers of attorney for personal care, advance directives, and living wills — learn the documents your jurisdiction uses and how to respond to a patient's wishes when the patient can no longer voice them.
atScene.zh: 许多省和地区都有关于个人照护授权书、预立指示和生前预嘱的立法——弄清你所在辖区用哪些文件，以及当患者已无法开口时，你该如何回应他预先留下的意愿。

atScene.en: Talk through when to start and when to stop CPR with your partner and crew before the moment arrives, so everyone understands the direction of the resuscitation.
atScene.zh: 什么时候开始、什么时候停止 CPR，要在事到临头之前就和搭档、车组谈透，让每个人都清楚这场复苏的走向。

atScene.en: Imagine facing a family emergency while visiting a foreign country — how hard would it be to trust a medical system different from everything you know? That is exactly how some of your patients feel about yours. Meet them with that in mind.
atScene.zh: 想象你在国外旅行时家人突发急症——要信任一个和你熟悉的一切都不同的医疗体系，有多难？你的一部分患者面对你的体系时，感受一模一样。带着这份体会去接他们。

atScene.en: The chapter case began with an AED whose battery had failed over a long weekend with nobody assigned to check it. Equipment checks are an ethical duty, not a chore — and when a failure happens, concealment is never an option: report it up to your supervisor and medical director.
atScene.zh: 本章案例的起点，是一台长周末无人负责检查、电池失效的 AED。查设备是伦理义务，不是杂务——而故障一旦发生，隐瞒永远不是选项：向主管和医疗主任如实上报。

confusions.en: Ethics versus morality versus law: ethics is the philosophy of right and wrong and ideal professional behaviour; morality is a conduct code defined by society, religion, or culture; law alone carries enforceable sanctions. An act can be legal yet unethical — and the reverse.
confusions.zh: 伦理、道德、法律三词打架：伦理是关于对错与理想职业行为的哲学；道德是由社会、宗教、文化定义的行为准则；只有法律带可强制执行的制裁。一件事可以合法却不合伦理——反过来也一样。

confusions.en: An advance directive is not a DNR order. The directive is the patient's expressed wishes that take effect on incapacity — it is what allows decisions like a DNR to be consented to; the DNR is a specific order about life-sustaining procedures when the heart or breathing stops.
confusions.zh: 预立指示不是 DNR 指令。指示是患者预先表达、失能后才生效的意愿——是让 DNR 这类决定得以被『同意』的依据；DNR 则是关于心跳或呼吸停止时是否施行维生操作的具体指令。

confusions.en: Beneficence versus nonmalfeasance: beneficence is actively doing what is best for the patient; nonmalfeasance is refraining from harm — primum non nocere. One commands action, the other restraint; the exam swaps their definitions to catch you.
confusions.zh: 行善与不伤害的错位：行善（beneficence）是主动做对患者最有利的事；不伤害（nonmalfeasance）是克制不造成伤害——primum non nocere。一个命令你出手，一个命令你收手；考题最爱把两个定义对调来钓人。

confusions.en: Persuasion is ethical; coercion and manipulation are not — and 'I was acting in his best interests' rescues neither. Honest concern persuades; threatening consequences coerces; distorting facts ('you'll die in the next 5 minutes') manipulates. The ends do not justify the means.
confusions.zh: 说服合乎伦理；胁迫和操纵不合——而『我是为他好』救不了后两者。真诚表达担忧是说服；拿后果要挟是胁迫；歪曲事实（『你五分钟内八成没命』）是操纵。目的不能为手段开脱。

confusions.en: A financial power of attorney or estate executor does not get health care decision power — only an attorney for personal care (substitute decision maker) does, and that person need not even be a relative.
confusions.zh: 财务授权代理人、遗产执行人≠医疗决策人——医疗决定只属于个人照护代理人（替代决策人），而这个人甚至不必是亲属。

confusions.en: A signed donor card does not settle organ donation: consent to donate is presented to the family, and a family refusal is respected even against the card — out of respect for the survivors. Know this before you promise a family 'his card decides.'
confusions.zh: 签了捐献卡不等于捐献已定：捐与不捐的同意要交给家属决定，家属拒绝时，即使与卡上意愿相反也被尊重——理由是尊重在世的家人。别在了解这一点之前对家属说『卡说了算』。

confusions.en: 'A slow code spares the family.' No — a deliberately slow, half-hearted resuscitation staged for onlookers is completely unethical. Resuscitate fully, or withhold/stop through direct medical control; the kind option is honesty plus support, not theatre.
confusions.zh: 『慢代码是给家属一个安慰。』——不。故意放慢、敷衍、演给旁人看的复苏彻底违背伦理。要么全力复苏，要么经直接医疗控制不启动或终止；真正仁慈的选项是诚实加陪伴，不是演戏。

confusions.en: 'Best interests' means what you would want for yourself? No — it is defined by the patient's own values, beliefs, and goals, weighed through the four-part test (values, benefit to condition or quality of life, benefits versus risks, less-intrusive alternatives). Your moral code is not the yardstick.
confusions.zh: 『最佳利益』＝你自己会怎么选？不——它由患者本人的价值观、信念与目标定义，经四步检验衡量（患者的价值观／能否改善病情或生活质量／收益是否大于风险／有无更低侵入的替代）。你的道德准则不是那把尺。

mnemonics.name: 四原则 ABNJ
mnemonics.en: Autonomy, Beneficence, Nonmalfeasance, Justice — 'All Bedside Nurses Judge fairly': respect the choice, do good, do no harm, share fairly.
mnemonics.zh: 自主、行善、不伤害、公正——记『自善无伤，公道在心』：尊重选择（自主）、主动做好事（行善）、收手不添害（不伤害）、资源分得公道（公正）。

mnemonics.name: 同意要 CIV
mnemonics.en: Ethically valid consent is CIVil: Capable (or a legal substitute), Informed, Voluntary — no coercion, no manipulation.
mnemonics.zh: 有效同意讲 CIV：Capable 有能力（或由法定替代人）、Informed 知情、Voluntary 自愿——没有胁迫，没有操纵。

mnemonics.name: 撤治五问
mnemonics.en: Stop or withhold treatment when: the patient/substitute Requests, Goals unmet, Not working, Burdens beat benefits (with consent), or Outside the standard of care.
mnemonics.zh: 五种情形可撤治，五问自查：本人（或替代人）提出了吗？预定目标落空了吗？治疗根本不起效吗？负担压过收益且对方同意吗？超出公认照护标准了吗？

mnemonics.name: MAID 五格
mnemonics.en: MAID eligibility: Insured in Canada, Adult 18+, Grievous and irremediable condition, Voluntary request, Informed consent — checked by two independent professionals.
mnemonics.zh: MAID 资格五格：加拿大医保内、年满 18、疾患严重不可挽回、请求自愿无压力、知情同意——再由两名独立专业人员核验。

selfCheck.qEn: Name and define the four principles of principlism, and say who proposed them and when.
selfCheck.qZh: 说出原则主义四原则并逐一定义；由谁、哪一年提出？
selfCheck.aEn: Beauchamp and Childress, 1979. Autonomy — respect people's right to make capable, informed decisions about their own care; beneficence — do what is best for the patient; nonmalfeasance — first, do no harm (primum non nocere); justice — fairness, treating equal cases equally and unequal cases unequally, including in resource distribution.
selfCheck.aZh: Beauchamp 与 Childress，1979 年。自主——尊重每个人对自身医疗作出有能力的知情决定的权利；行善——做对患者最有利的事；不伤害——首先不伤害（primum non nocere）；公正——公平，相同情形同等对待、不同情形区别对待，包括资源分配。

selfCheck.qEn: State the three ethical conditions of valid consent, and the standard for how much information makes consent 'informed.'
selfCheck.qZh: 有效同意的三个伦理条件是什么？信息给到多少才算『知情』，标准是什么？
selfCheck.aEn: Capable patient (or legal substitute decision maker if incapable); informed; voluntary — free of coercion and manipulation. 'Enough' information is what a reasonable person in the patient's circumstances would expect, plus real opportunity and time to ask questions.
selfCheck.aZh: 患者有能力（无能力时由法定替代决策人）；知情；自愿——不受胁迫与操纵。信息量的标准是『处于患者境地的理性人会期望知道什么』，还要给出真正的提问机会和时间。

selfCheck.qEn: Give one example each of persuasion, coercion, and manipulation with a reluctant chest-pain patient. Which are unethical?
selfCheck.qZh: 对一名不肯就医的胸痛患者，各举一例说服、胁迫、操纵。哪些不合伦理？
selfCheck.aEn: Persuasion (ethical): 'I really feel you should come to the hospital — we are all concerned about you.' Coercion (unethical): 'If you don't come, we'll never respond to your 9-1-1 call again.' Manipulation (unethical): 'If you don't come, chances are great you'll die in the next 5 minutes.' Good intentions change nothing — the ends do not justify the means.
selfCheck.aZh: 说服（合伦理）：『我真的觉得你该去医院，我们都很担心你。』胁迫（不合）：『你不去，以后打 911 我们就再也不来了。』操纵（不合）：『你不去，五分钟内八成就没命了。』出发点再好也没用——目的不能为手段开脱。

selfCheck.qEn: List the five circumstances under which treatment may be withheld or withdrawn.
selfCheck.qZh: 列出可以不给或撤除治疗的五种情形。
selfCheck.aEn: (1) The patient or substitute decision maker requests it; (2) the treatment has not attained its preset goals; (3) the treatment is not working; (4) burdens exceed benefits and the patient or substitute consents; (5) the treatment falls outside a well-recognized, accepted standard of prehospital care. When in doubt, contact the medical oversight physician.
selfCheck.aZh: ①患者或替代决策人请求；②治疗未达预定目标；③治疗不起作用；④负担大于收益且患者或替代决策人同意；⑤治疗超出公认的院前照护标准。拿不准就联系医疗监督医生。

selfCheck.qEn: MAID under Bill C-14: the five eligibility criteria, the four components of 'grievous and irremediable,' and the assessment requirement.
selfCheck.qZh: C-14 法案下的 MAID：五项资格标准、『严重且不可挽回』的四个构件、以及评估要求。
selfCheck.aEn: Criteria: government-funded health insurance eligibility in Canada; age 18+; grievous and irremediable condition; voluntary request without external pressure; informed consent after being told of suffering-relief options including palliative care. Grievous and irremediable: serious incurable illness/disease/disability; advanced irreversible decline in capability; intolerable physical and psychological suffering; reasonably foreseeable natural death. Assessment: two independent health care professionals, with the person still capable of informed consent when MAID is performed.
selfCheck.aZh: 五标准：有资格享受加拿大政府资助医保；年满 18 岁；严重且不可挽回的疾患；自愿请求、无外部压力；被告知包括姑息治疗在内的减痛手段后给出知情同意。四构件：严重且无法治愈的疾病或残障；能力不可逆衰退的晚期；本人无法忍受的身心痛苦；自然死亡可合理预见。评估要求：两名独立医疗专业人员，且执行当下本人仍具知情同意能力。

selfCheck.qEn: A deceased patient carries a signed donor card; the family refuses donation. What happens, and what is the paramedic's role in field donation conversations?
selfCheck.qZh: 死者签有捐献卡，家属却拒绝捐献。结果如何？救护员在现场捐献对话中的角色是什么？
selfCheck.aEn: The family's refusal is respected, even against the signed card — out of respect for the survivors. The paramedic never judges organ viability; under a service protocol (field-terminated or non-attempted resuscitation, criteria met), the role is to inform next of kin that donation is an option, hand over an information card, notify the medical examiner or tissue service — and never pressure the family.
selfCheck.aZh: 尊重家属的拒绝，即使违背卡上意愿——理由是尊重在世家人。救护员从不判断器官是否可用；在本服务有协议（复苏已现场终止或未启动、各项标准满足）时，角色只是：告知近亲捐献是一个选项、递上信息卡、通知法医或组织捐献机构——并且绝不施压。

selfCheck.qEn: A colleague tells you privately that another paramedic destroyed call evidence, and fears retaliation. What must you do?
selfCheck.qZh: 同事私下告诉你另一名救护员销毁了出勤证据，他自己又怕被报复。你必须怎么做？
selfCheck.aEn: Report the information immediately to your supervisor and medical program director so corrective action can begin; keep the informant's name private and tell him honestly what steps you must take while protecting his identity. Staying silent would make you a party to the misconduct — the duty to disclose runs to your patients, community, and profession.
selfCheck.aZh: 立即向主管和医疗项目主任报告，让纠正程序启动；为线人保密，并坦诚告知他你必须走的程序、承诺保护他的身份。保持沉默就等于成为不当行为的同伙——揭露的义务对象是你的患者、社区和职业。

bcAlerts.topicEn: MAID law has moved on since this textbook edition
bcAlerts.topicZh: MAID 的法律在教材成书后已经前进
bcAlerts.bookEn: The book presents Bill C-14 (2016), under which a 'reasonably foreseeable natural death' is one of the four components of a grievous and irremediable condition.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材呈现的是 2016 年的 C-14 法案，其中『自然死亡可合理预见』是『严重且不可挽回』的四构件之一。
bcAlerts.bcEn: Federal Bill C-7 (2021) amended the Criminal Code to remove the reasonably-foreseeable-death requirement as an eligibility bar, creating a two-track safeguard system (one track for those whose natural death is reasonably foreseeable, a stricter track for those whose death is not). For exam purposes learn the textbook's C-14 framework — but do not be surprised if practice documents reflect the newer law.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 联邦 C-7 法案（2021 年）修订《刑法典》，取消了『自然死亡可合理预见』这一资格门槛，改为双轨保障制（死亡可预见者一轨，不可预见者适用更严的一轨）。备考以教材的 C-14 框架为准——但在实务文件里看到新法的写法不要意外。
bcAlerts.ref: 通行法律知识，非考纲内容

bcAlerts.topicEn: Where misconduct complaints land in BC
bcAlerts.topicZh: 在 BC，行为不端的投诉落到哪里
bcAlerts.bookEn: The chapter tells you to report colleague misconduct 'up the appropriate chain of command' and medical errors to the medical director, leaving the regulator unnamed.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 本章只说同事不当行为要『沿指挥链上报』、医疗差错报医疗主任，没有点名监管机构。
bcAlerts.bcEn: In BC the licensing body with investigative and disciplinary power over EMRs and paramedics is the Emergency Medical Assistants Licensing Board (EMALB), acting under the Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation (B.C. Reg. 210/2010). Falsified certification, practice outside licence conditions, and serious misconduct can all end in EMALB licence action — the due-process mechanics are the ones described in Chapter 4.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 在 BC，对 EMR 和救护员握有调查与惩戒权的发照机构是紧急医疗助理发照委员会（EMALB），依据《紧急医疗助理条例》（B.C. Reg. 210/2010）行事。伪造认证、超出执照条件执业、严重不当行为都可能招致 EMALB 的执照处分——正当程序的流程见第 4 章所述。
bcAlerts.ref: EMALB 官方规定；Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation, B.C. Reg. 210/2010（BC Laws）
